segments.en: Everyone tries to contribute as much as possible so that when you retire, you can rest peacefully on your nest egg.
segments.zh: 大家都尽量多存一点，这样退休后就能靠这笔积蓄安心养老。

segments.en: That's interesting and logical, I guess.
segments.zh: 我猜这很有趣和合乎逻辑。

segments.en: In my country, we also have to contribute to a government-run retirement fund, but most people don't really trust it, so they just invest in properties or things like that.
segments.zh: 在我的国家，我们还必须为政府经营的退休基金捐款，但大多数人并不真正信任它，所以他们只投资于房产或类似的东西。

segments.en: That seems a bit unstable, don't you think?
segments.zh: 这似乎有点不稳定，你不觉得吗？

segments.en: Yeah, but corrupt governments in the past have created distrust among banks and financial institutions, so now people prefer to have money hidden in a jar or a piggy bank.
segments.zh: 是的，但过去的腐败政府在银行和金融机构之间造成了不信任，所以现在人们更喜欢把钱藏在罐子或存钱罐里。

segments.en: I've been thinking of doing that lately.
segments.zh: 我最近一直在想这样做。

segments.en: I don't want some banker to run off with my money.
segments.zh: 我不想让一些银行家带着我的钱逃跑。

segments.en: Alright, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So this whole savings thing, are you good at saving?
segments.zh: 那么这整个储蓄的事情，你擅长储蓄吗？

segments.en: Do you have your nest egg planned out for your retirement?
segments.zh: 你有没有为退休规划好你的积蓄？

segments.en: Nest egg, no, but I'm a compulsive saver.
segments.zh: 积蓄，不，不过我是个存钱上瘾的人。

segments.en: Really?
segments.zh: 真的吗？

segments.en: I like to save a lot.
segments.zh: 我很喜欢存钱。

segments.en: Oh, wow.
segments.zh: 哦，哇。

segments.en: Yeah, because you never know when you're going to need money.
segments.zh: 是的，因为你永远不知道什么时候需要钱。

segments.en: And I think once you get a kind of an adult job, you know, the nine to five job, it's important to spend as little as possible so that you can create a nest egg or some kind of savings account for the future because it'd be nice to have a car or a house someday.
segments.zh: 而且我认为，一旦你找到一份成人工作，你知道，朝九晚五的工作，重要的是尽可能少花钱，这样你就可以为未来创建一个储备金或某种储蓄账户，因为有一天有一辆车或一所房子会很好。

segments.en: Right, right.
segments.zh: 对，对。

segments.en: And also, as you say, unexpected things happen.
segments.zh: 而且，正如你所说，意想不到的事情发生了。

segments.en: So something may happen.
segments.zh: 所以可能会发生一些事情。

segments.en: Maybe you break your arm and you don't have any savings or maybe no insurance.
segments.zh: 也许你摔断了手臂，你没有任何积蓄，也没有保险。

segments.en: So at least you have some money stashed away where you can use it.
segments.zh: 所以至少你存了一些钱可以拿来用。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: And I know that in America right now, in the news, the credit crisis is very popular to talk about.
segments.zh: 而且我知道，在美国，信贷危机是新闻里热议的话题。

segments.en: And so part of this economic situation is that people owe more money than they have.
segments.zh: 因此，这种经济状况的一部分就是人们欠的钱比拥有的还多。

segments.en: That means they've spent more money than they own.
segments.zh: 这意味着他们花费的钱比他们拥有的要多。

segments.en: And so they don't have any savings.
segments.zh: 所以他们没有任何积蓄。

segments.en: And that really scares me.
segments.zh: 这真的让我害怕。

segments.en: So I think it's a really smart idea to start investing as soon as you can.
segments.zh: 所以我认为尽快开始投资是一个非常明智的想法。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.zh: 来自 Englishpod.com 的明智财务建议。

segments.en: Thank you.
segments.zh: 谢谢。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.zh: 因此，如果您有任何问题、任何疑问或任何其他财务问题，请访问 englishpod.com，我们将在那里见到你们。

segments.en: Bye, everyone.
segments.zh: 大家再见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
